title: MOOR Recursive Funnel Fabric
purpose: A recursively composable, evidence-aware, solver-driven Funnel system that can expand by configuration and resources instead of by rewriting architecture.
originalIntent: Design the Funnel system itself so it captures the entire emerging model: immutable Page 0; open-ended non-leading questions; literal Sebastian evidence kept distinct from proposed solutions; parallel Sebastian solver workers who independently answer questions framed as direct questions from Sebastian; deliberate synthetic certainty from independent agreeing solution ballots; recursive sub-funnels for unresolved requirements; reusable packaged Funnel systems; 3D topology editing and deterministic reassembly; receipts and replay; iterative architecture experiments; verification and learning; and scaling limited primarily by configured compute/storage/retention rather than a fixed topology.
governingPrinciples: One small kernel defines law; almost everything else is data, packages, workers or configuration.
Questions seek answers; they do not smuggle in preferred solutions.
Sebastian solver workers solve questions for Sebastian. They do not impersonate Sebastian or rewrite owner history.
Independent agreeing solver ballots intentionally increase synthetic solution confidence.
Literal owner evidence and solver consensus are separate confidence channels.
A repeated retrieval of one owner statement remains one owner fact; repeated independent solution attempts may be multiple solver votes.
Every unresolved material question may spawn a child Funnel with narrower scope.
Every child Funnel returns a compact receipt to its parent; parents do not need the child's full working set after compaction.
The logical graph is primary. 3D geometry is a renderer/editor for that graph, never the source of truth.
Resource limits are parameters and warnings, not architectural ceilings.
No amount of consensus substitutes for execution verification.

nonResponsibilities: hard-code a maximum number of funnels

runtimePipeline: reference retrieval and locked owner facts

systems.job: Convert unresolved requirements into neutral open-ended questions.
invariants: Do not imply a preferred answer.
Ask only questions whose answers can materially change the blueprint or execution.
Attach why_material so the system can later prove the question was worth asking.

systems.job: Spawn N isolated solution workers per question, each receiving the question as a direct request from Sebastian.
invariants: Workers cannot see peer ballots before submitting.
Each ballot is a proposed solution, not an owner statement.
Multiple agreeing ballots intentionally count as multiple solver votes.

systems.job: Maintain literal Sebastian statements, corrections, locks and scoped preferences separately from solver proposals.
invariants: Same source retrieved N times does not become N owner facts.
Corrections can supersede older evidence without deleting history.
Scope is explicit so local preferences do not silently become global laws.

systems.job: Transform free-form ballots into comparable propositions before voting.
systems.design: Use structured ballot fields first; use a semantic normalizer only when wording differs enough that deterministic matching is insufficient.
systems.output: canonical propositions with supporting and opposing ballot IDs

systems.job: Turn independent solution ballots into transparent synthetic decision confidence.

confidenceChannels.owner: How strongly literal Sebastian evidence establishes a choice.
confidenceChannels.solver: How strongly independent solution attempts converge.
confidenceChannels.verification: How strongly observed execution proves the choice worked.

systems.rule: Solver consensus may authorize a provisional design decision when policy permits, but it never rewrites owner evidence.

systems.job: Create child FunnelCases for requirements/questions whose uncertainty or complexity exceeds the current case.
systems.scalingRule: No fixed architectural depth. Runtime budgets provide the practical limit and may be raised as resources grow.
termination: verification required instead of more reasoning

systems.job: Return compact, content-addressed receipts from every significant child decision to its parent.
behavior: Child working sets may be ephemeral.
Parent stores the child verdict/receipt plus content hash.
Full traces can be retained selectively for debugging/training.
Compaction may replace old working receipts with a summary root while preserving auditability.

systems.job: Store reusable high-level Funnel systems as declarative graph packages.
Procedurally edit complete Funnel ecosystems as graphs.
Make scale physically legible before execution.
systems.rule: Red means expensive/risky, not forbidden. The user may raise the budget or proceed deliberately.

systems.job: Replay the same historical request corpus through candidate Funnel architectures and compare results.
systems.promotionRule: A candidate Funnel architecture becomes production law only through explicit promotion after regression comparison.

systems.job: Learn which workers, lenses, questions and consensus patterns predict verified outcomes.
systems.rule: Train weights on observed outcomes/corrections, not on model confidence alone.

systems.job: Store raw personal requests and owner evidence privately.
systems.separation: Code/templates may live in GitHub; raw personal ledger does not need to.

systems.job: Render the logical topology as points, lines, cones and packages for inspection/editing.
systems.rule: Geometry carries spatial organization; logical edges remain finite explicit relationships.

scalability.model: recursive fan-out / fan-in over declarative graph packages
scalability.horizontalScale: Workers and child FunnelCases are stateless jobs addressable by IDs and can run across additional processes/machines.
scalability.persistence: Append-only event/receipt logs can be sharded by case/date/project and compacted.
scalability.cache: Locked decisions, normalized propositions and verified package outputs are reusable by content hash.
scalability.backpressure: Resource governor throttles creation when configured budgets are reached.
scalability.theoreticalLimit: No fixed limit encoded in topology. Practical limits are address space, scheduler throughput, model/context limits, storage, compute, network and cost.

failureContainment: Child failure cannot mutate parent Page 0.
A failed child returns a failure receipt rather than poisoning sibling state.
A consensus loop cannot recurse indefinitely without consuming an explicit budget.
A popular solver answer is not treated as owner truth.
A valid graph is not treated as proof of semantic correctness.
A successful build is not treated as proof of intent satisfaction.

foundryResourceModel.visual: Continuously show green/yellow/red budget pressure before Reassemble and before Run.

initialDefaults.owner_interrupt_policy: Only material contradiction, unsupported owner-only decision, or budget/promotion decision.
initialDefaults.ballot_retention: compact after verified outcome; retain representative disagreements and failures

doneCriteria: The actual Funnel kernel can issue a valid receipt for this blueprint request.
The system can spawn multiple isolated solver ballots for one open-ended question without relabeling them as owner evidence.
Agreeing solver ballots raise synthetic confidence and owner evidence remains a distinct field.
Any unresolved material question can create a child FunnelCase and return a receipt to its parent.
No fixed code change is required to increase worker count, branch factor, recursion depth or package multiplicity within supported numeric/storage limits.
Resource projections are available before recursive expansion.
The Foundry can serialize, reassemble, compare and explicitly promote topology experiments.
Historical requests can be replayed against candidate architectures for regression/calibration.
Production execution still requires Page 0 replay, receipt validation and downstream verification.
